summary: This is a Makefile that defines a simple target called 'hello' which prints 'Hello World' to the console. The 'default' target points to 'hello', so running 'make' without arguments will execute the hello target by default.

explanations.1: The 'default' target specifies which target should run if you just type 'make' with no arguments — in this case, it will run the 'hello' target.
explanations.3: This line defines a target named 'hello' that can be invoked by running 'make hello'.
explanations.4: The '@' symbol suppresses echoing the command itself to the console, so only the output 'Hello World' is shown, not the echo command. The indentation must be a tab character, not spaces, because that's how Makefiles distinguish commands from other lines.
